question.worked_solution:
To find ${f}^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y:$

$$
y=\frac{3k}{6+4x}
$$

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

$$
x=\frac{3k}{6+4y}.
$$

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{3k}{6+4y} \\ x & =\frac{3k}{6+4y} \\ x(6+4y) & =3k \\ 6x+4xy & =3k \\ 4xy & =3k-6x \\ y & =\frac{3k-6x}{4x}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the inverse function is 

$$
{f}^{-1}(x)=\frac{3k-6x}{4x}.
$$

Comparing our answer with the given expression, we conclude that $k=3.$
